_about: Words for the Traveler tab's game (Where in the World Was Deo?): what Deo says from the hammock, and fun facts he shares after some answers. Each fact's key is a place key (jp-13 = Tokyo, us-mn = Minnesota: the country code, then the state/province folder's code) or a country code (applies to all its places). No famous people, no sports.
chatter: I like to take my time too, but I hope you're not doing something Ecchi while staring at me huehue...
Take your time. This hammock has no hard commitments.
Pro tip: check the signs, the plugs and which side of the road the cars drive on.
I took these photos and I still squint at some of them.
Zzz… huh? Oh, you're still here. Good, good.
Remember: one freebie per game. Use it wisely.
If you miss this one, I'm telling Peeta.
Every wrong answer is just a trip you still have to take.
Huehue, I can feel that thinking face from here.

facts.text: Shinjuku Station in Tokyo is the busiest train station in the world: millions of people pass through it every day.
Osaka's food motto is kuidaore: eat until you drop (or go broke). Challenge accepted.
Fukuoka has more yatai, open-air food stalls, than the rest of Japan combined: about a hundred pop up every night and vanish before morning.
Hong Kong has more skyscrapers than any other city in the world.
China is wide enough for five time zones, but the whole country runs on one clock: Beijing time.
Kuala Lumpur's Petronas Towers were the tallest buildings in the world from 1998 to 2004, and a two-story skybridge joins them.
Singapore's Changi Airport has the tallest indoor waterfall in the world, the Rain Vortex. An airport with a waterfall: my aviation nerd heart.
Bangkok's full ceremonial name is the longest place name in the world. Locals just call it Krung Thep.
Da Nang's Dragon Bridge breathes fire, and then water, on weekend nights. Yes, a bridge. Yes, fire.
Near Da Nang, the Golden Bridge in the Ba Na Hills is held up by two giant stone hands.
Germany's Reinheitsgebot, the beer purity law of 1516, allowed only water, barley and hops in beer.
Spain makes more olive oil than any other country in the world.
The Eiffel Tower grows about 15 cm in summer, because its iron expands in the heat.
The London Underground opened in 1863: the oldest underground railway in the world.
Venice is built on more than a hundred small islands, linked by around 400 bridges.
Vatican City is the smallest country in the world: less than half a square kilometer.
In the Exumas, in the Bahamas, there's a beach where pigs swim out to meet the boats.
Minnesota calls itself the Land of 10,000 Lakes, but it actually has more than 11,000.
North Dakota's Enchanted Highway is lined with giant scrap-metal sculptures, and Geese in Flight is the largest scrap-metal sculpture in the world.
In Tonopah, Nevada, there's a motel full of clowns, right next to an old miners' cemetery. Sweet dreams!
Death Valley holds the hottest air temperature ever recorded on Earth: 56.7 °C (134 °F), back in 1913.
Under a bridge in Seattle lives the Fremont Troll, a giant concrete troll crushing a real Volkswagen Beetle.
At Cadillac Ranch in Amarillo, Texas, ten Cadillacs stand nose-down in the dirt, and spray-painting them is encouraged.
Chicago reversed the flow of its river in 1900, so it runs away from Lake Michigan instead of into it. Engineering flex.
Denver is the Mile High City: one step of the Colorado State Capitol sits exactly one mile above sea level.
Nashville has a full-size replica of the Parthenon of Athens.
Iowa has more pigs than people. Many, many more.
The Everglades in Florida are the only place in the world where alligators and crocodiles live side by side.
Brazil is the only country in the Americas whose main language is Portuguese.
Macapá, the capital of Amapá, sits right on the equator, and the Marco Zero monument marks the line.
Rio Grande do Sul is gaúcho country: the home of churrasco and chimarrão, the bitter mate tea sipped from a gourd.
Recife, in Pernambuco, is nicknamed the Brazilian Venice for its rivers and bridges.
Brasília was built from scratch in about four years, and from above its city plan looks like an airplane.
